colors.name: Crimson Seal
colors.role: Primary action - filled add-to-cart buttons, CTA borders, section eyebrows, price accents, link underlines, and all brand punctuation against the cream canvas. The red carries the entire chromatic load; it must read as deliberate and small, never as decoration

colors.name: Vermillion Mark
colors.role: Secondary red accent - link borders, icon strokes, and outline-only controls. Slightly deeper than Crimson Seal; use when a quieter red moment is needed alongside the primary

colors.name: Ink Black
colors.role: Primary text, primary borders, navigation rules, body hairlines. The structural anchor of the entire interface

colors.name: Soft Coal
colors.role: Badge borders, heading text, list markers, card text on cream - a near-black used where pure black would feel clinical against the warm canvas

colors.name: Slate Drift
colors.role: Navigation borders, secondary structural lines - sits between Ink Black and the warm cream as a third depth

colors.name: Graphite
colors.role: Body text and borders for muted but still-readable paragraphs

colors.name: Pewter
colors.role: Badge borders, helper text, muted body copy - the first true mid-gray in the scale

colors.name: Stone
colors.role: Warm-leaning gray for tags, secondary body text, and quiet fills where neutrality needs to harmonize with the cream

colors.name: Sand Border
colors.role: Warm button borders, subtle section dividers - the border color that ties the warm palette together instead of fighting it with cool gray

colors.name: Cream Paper
colors.role: Page canvas, badge fills, soft card surfaces - the dominant background. Slightly warm to harmonize with product photography of amber liquids

colors.name: Pure Linen
colors.role: Card surfaces, button text on red, elevated product panels - the brightest surface that sits one step above the cream canvas

colors.name: Blush Wash
colors.role: Soft accent badge fills, warm callout backgrounds - a desaturated peach that gives badge states a skin-like warmth

fonts.name: Soehne Buch
fonts.role: Primary body face at comfortable reading sizes (13-16px). Cleaner, more humanist than Nimbus; used for longer paragraphs and form input text.

fonts.name: Nimbus Sans
fonts.role: Workhorse sans for UI: button labels, body copy, price text, nav links, and all utility surfaces. Carries lnum/tnum features for tabular alignment of prices.

fonts.name: Soehne Kraftig
fonts.role: Display and small-bold sans for headlines (60px), navigation, and tracked uppercase labels (11-12px with 0.07-0.10em tracking). The Kraftig cut adds authority without geometric coldness.

fonts.name: AGaramondPro
fonts.role: Editorial serif for major section headlines (54px) and subheadings (17-26px). The Garamond weight gives the brand its apothecary/editorial voice; pairs with italic for emotional accents.

fonts.name: Garamond Italic
fonts.role: Signature italic for emotional phrases, pull quotes, and editorial interjections mid-paragraph. Used sparingly - it is a whisper, not a shout.

fonts.name: EB Garamond
fonts.role: EB Garamond - detected in extracted data but not described by AI

components.name: Primary Action Button (Add to Cart)
components.role: Filled CTA for purchase and primary conversion

components.name: Outlined CTA (Shop the Elixir)
components.role: Secondary hero action with red border

components.name: Ghost Text Link
components.role: Inline editorial links and story links

components.name: Product Card
components.role: E-commerce product tile with image, name, benefit, price, CTA

components.name: Section Eyebrow Label
components.role: Red uppercase tracked label introducing sections

components.name: Editorial Italic Pull-Quote
components.role: Garamond italic phrase embedded in or near headlines

components.name: Top Announcement Bar
components.role: Free-shipping message strip across the top

components.name: Header Navigation
components.role: Primary site navigation with centered logo

components.name: Comparison Card
components.role: Two-column comparison block (typical vs. Isla system)

components.name: Price with Sale
components.role: Inline pricing with original and sale value

components.name: Soft Badge
components.role: Tag or status badge with warm fill

do: Use #e4263d exclusively as the brand red - never substitute another red, and never tint or lighten it for non-critical contexts.
Pair Garamond italic #e4263d phrases with sans body copy when you want editorial emphasis.
Set all uppercase micro-labels (10-12px) at letter-spacing 0.12-0.18em in Nimbus Sans 500.
Use 3px radius for every rectangular component - cards, buttons, inputs, images. Reserve 999px exclusively for pills/tags.
Set the page canvas to #f8f6f3 (cream), not #ffffff. White appears only on cards, buttons, and product images.
Anchor every section with a red eyebrow label (Nimbus 11px uppercase, 0.18em) before the headline.
Use hairline 1px borders in #000000 or #e4dfd9 - never 2px+ and never with shadows.
doNot: Don't introduce drop shadows, glow effects, or elevation layers - the design is intentionally flat.
Don't use cool grays (blue-tinted). All neutrals should sit in the warm spectrum (#6f6f6f, #8a8580, #e4dfd9).
Don't round corners beyond 3px on rectangular components; the system is sharp with intentional restraint.
Don't mix more than one serif in the same paragraph. Garamond Italic is punctuation, not body type.
Don't use red as a fill area larger than a button - red is a seal, not a field.
Don't set body copy below 13px or above 17px. The 13-17px range is the system's comfort zone.
Don't use #000000 for anything other than primary text and primary borders. For surfaces and secondary text, move to #1a1a1a or #3a3a3a.
